msedge-tts 0.4.0 vendored from crates.io, with TWO local modifications.
Source:   https://github.com/hs-CN/msedge-tts  (crates.io msedge-tts 0.4.0, published 2026-05-20)
Checksum: c5ee3d00bfd237fac2dcd03050c073d60769c9d1f2718545854374f1aa4d6d5b (crates.io .crate, as recorded in
          Cargo.lock before vendoring)
License:  MIT OR Apache-2.0 (see ./LICENSE)
Wired in: src-tauri/Cargo.toml [patch.crates-io] — the dependency declaration itself is unchanged.

Copied:   Cargo.toml, LICENSE, README.md, src/ — byte-identical to the published crate except the two changes
          below. Nothing else from the package is needed to build it.

Sard does not use this crate's own synthesis request. It builds the request itself — the route, the
Sec-MS-GEC token and the headers — in src-tauri/src/tts/edge_route.rs and edge_token.rs, and opens it
through MODIFICATION 1. Everything else this crate does is used as published: the TLS connection, the
synthesis protocol (speech.config + ssml messages, the turn.start / response / audio.metadata / turn.end
replies) and the voice list.


=== MODIFICATION 1: A CONNECTION MADE WITH THE CALLER'S REQUEST =====================================

src/tts/mod.rs: the body of `websocket_connect` becomes `websocket_connect_request(request)`, which takes
the upgrade request as an argument instead of building it; `websocket_connect` now calls it with
`build_websocket_request()`, so the crate's own entry points behave exactly as published.
src/tts/stream/blocking.rs: one added function beside `msedge_tts_split` —

  pub fn msedge_tts_split_request(request) -> Result<(Sender<TcpStream>, Receiver<TcpStream>)>

the same split client over a connection made with the given request.

WHY. The crate hard-codes the host, the token scheme and the headers of the request, and the service has
changed what it accepts twice in two weeks:

  * from 2026-10-10 the original host refuses the version-1 token this crate generates (HTTP 403). Sard
    1.4.1 answered that by moving to the other host, which still accepted it;
  * from 2026-10-23 that other host answers a WebSocket request carrying neither Accept nor
    Accept-Encoding — which this crate's request does not carry — with a plain HTTP 200 instead of
    upgrading it. Read-aloud stopped completely. Measured 2026-10-24 with Sard 1.4.1's own client: 0 of 5
    connections, every one answered 200; the same request with Accept-Encoding added: upgraded.

With the request in Sard's hands, a change of host, token or header is a change to Sard's own code, and
Sard can keep more than one route (see edge_route.rs for the routes, how a refused one is stepped around,
and the measurements behind each). A later release of this crate (0.4.1) also generates the version-2
token, but it moves back to a single hard-coded host; this copy stays at 0.4.0 and takes the request
instead.


=== MODIFICATION 2: KEEP-ALIVE FRAMES ===============================================================

src/tts/mod.rs, `Payload::process`: one match arm, before the catch-all —

  tungstenite::Message::Ping(_) | tungstenite::Message::Pong(_) => Ok(None),

WHY. The catch-all turns every frame other than text, binary and close into
`UnexpectedMessage("unexpected message: ")`, which fails the synthesis being read. The original host was
never seen sending such frames (no such failure among the production requests recorded before 2026-10-10);
the other one does. Measured 2026-10-12 on one held connection: an unsolicited, empty Pong
about every 120 s (at 120.5 s and 240.5 s), and in the application the same error 2.3 minutes into a
listening session — one failed synthesis and one reconnect per two minutes of continuous reading.
A keep-alive frame carries no synthesis data, and tungstenite answers a Ping by itself, so both now yield
no payload. The turn's state is untouched and every other frame keeps its handling.


=== NO LONGER MODIFIED ==============================================================================

src/constants.rs is the published file again. It carried Sard's first change (the synthesis host, from
2026-10-12); the host is now chosen by Sard's own request, so the crate's constant is no longer read for
synthesis and was restored. VOICE_LIST_URL, which the voice list still uses, was never changed.

src/tts/mod.rs, `build_websocket_request`, carries no header change. PR #66 (Basil Alrashedi) found the
2026-10-23 cause independently — the msedge host answers a handshake without Accept-Encoding with a plain
HTTP 200 — and fixed it first, by adding Accept-Encoding and Accept-Language to this crate's own request.
That request is no longer used for synthesis: Sard's request (src-tauri/src/tts/edge_route.rs) sends the
same two headers, so the lines are carried there instead of being kept here as a second, unused copy.


=== RE-VENDORING / REMOVING ========================================================================

Remove this directory and the [patch.crates-io] entry once an upstream msedge-tts release can connect with
a request the caller builds and handles keep-alive frames. To re-vendor: copy the four items above from
the new published crate, re-apply the changes still needed, update this file, and check the copy against
the published crate file by file — the only expected differences are the ones recorded here.
tests/unit/ttsEndpoint.test.ts pins both changes, that synthesis goes through Sard's own request, and every
other byte of the copy against the published crate.
